question: As a compliance officer at a private sector bank, how far in advance must we submit a proposal for appointing a new MD&CEO to the RBI?
answer: The proposal must be submitted at least four months before the expiry of the term of the present incumbent.
evidence: A proposal for appointment of a new MD&CEO / CEO shall invariably contain a panel of at least two names in the order of preference and shall be submitted to RBI at least four months before the expiry of the term of office of the present incumbent.

question: Under the RBI’s 2025 Directions, what policy and approval requirements apply when a commercial bank sets interest rates on foreign-currency advances?
answer: The bank must follow a comprehensive policy on interest rates on advances that has been duly approved by its Board of Directors or a Board committee to which the Board has delegated powers.
evidence: A bank shall have the freedom to determine the interest rates on advances in foreign currency as per the comprehensive policy on interest rates on advances duly approved by the Board of Directors or any committee of the Board to which powers have been delegated.

question: Can a commercial bank apply different tenor premiums to different borrowers or loan categories for the same residual tenor?
answer: No, the tenor premium must be uniform across all loan types for a given residual tenor and cannot vary by borrower or loan class.
evidence: The change in tenor premium should not be borrower specific or loan class specific. In other words, the tenor premium will be uniform for all types of loans for a given residual tenor.

question: For a commercial bank, do the interest-rate directions in paragraph 6 also apply to rupee advances granted against FCNR(B) deposits for a third party?
answer: Yes. Those directions also apply to rupee advances made against FCNR(B) deposits for a third party.
evidence: The directions contained in paragraph 6 above shall also be applicable to Rupee advances granted against FCNR(B) deposits to a third party or out of resources mobilised under the FCNR(B) scheme.

question: What reference rates qualify as an external benchmark rate for a commercial bank under the RBI's 2025 interest rate directions?
answer: An external benchmark rate includes the RBI policy repo rate, Government of India three-month and six-month treasury bill yields published by FBIL, or any other benchmark market interest rate published by FBIL.
evidence: ‘External benchmark rate’ means the reference rate which includes: 1. Reserve Bank of India policy Repo Rate; 2. Government of India Three-months and Six-months Treasury Bill yields published by Financial Benchmarks India Private Ltd (FBIL); 3. Any other benchmark market interest rate published by FBIL.

question: As a commercial bank, how often must we reset the interest rate on advances that are linked to an external benchmark?
answer: A commercial bank must reset the interest rate under an external benchmark at least once every three months.
evidence: The interest rate under external benchmark shall be reset at least once in three months.

question: What must a commercial bank's Board-approved policy on spread charged to customers include?
answer: The policy must delineate the components of spread and include principles to determine the quantum of each component, the range of spread for borrower categories or loan types, and the delegation of loan pricing powers.
evidence: A bank shall have a Board approved policy delineating the components of spread charged to a customer. The policy shall include principles: 1. To determine the quantum of each component of spread. 2. To determine the range of spread for a given category of borrower / type of loan. 3. To delegate powers in respect of loan pricing.

question: Our commercial bank had already initiated steps to sanction a loan and set its interest rate under the RBI's earlier interest-rate directions before those directions were repealed. Which set of rules continues to govern that in-progress action?
answer: The earlier directions continue to govern any action taken, purportedly taken, or initiated under them before the repeal, so the bank's in-progress steps remain subject to the old provisions rather than the new ones.
evidence: Notwithstanding such repeal, any action taken or purported to have been taken, or initiated under the repealed Directions, instructions, or guidelines shall continue to be governed by the provisions thereof.

question: For a commercial bank, which MCLR applies to a loan when the first disbursement is only partial?
answer: The MCLR prevailing on the date of that first partial disbursement applies until the next reset date, even if the benchmark changes before then.
evidence: The MCLR prevailing on the date of first disbursement, whether partial or full, shall be applicable till the next reset date, irrespective of the changes in the benchmark during the interim.

question: How often must a commercial bank reassess its Base Rate?
answer: A commercial bank must review its Base Rate at least once in every quarter.
evidence: A bank shall review the Base Rate at least once in a quarter with the approval of the Board or the Asset Liability Management Committees (ALCOs) as per the bank’s practice.

question: What governance requirement must a commercial bank meet regarding its interest rate policy on advances?
answer: A commercial bank must have a comprehensive policy on interest rates on advances, including microfinance loan pricing, approved by its Board of Directors or a delegated committee.
evidence: There shall be a comprehensive policy duly approved by the Board of Directors or any committee of the Board to which powers have been delegated, in respect of interest rates on advances, including the pricing of microfinance loans.

question: Which methods can a commercial bank use to calculate its cost of funds for the internal benchmark, and what standards must the chosen method meet?
answer: A commercial bank may calculate cost of funds on the basis of average cost of funds, marginal cost of funds, or any other reasonable and transparent methodology in vogue. The method must be applied consistently and be made available for supervisory review or scrutiny as and when required.
evidence: A bank shall have the freedom to calculate cost of funds either on the basis of average cost of funds or on marginal cost of funds or any other methodology in vogue, which is reasonable and transparent, subject to it being consistent and made available for supervisory review / scrutiny as and when required.

question: For a commercial bank, do existing loans and credit limits linked to the Base Rate or BPLR automatically convert to MCLR, or do they remain under the old benchmark?
answer: Existing loans and credit limits linked to the Base Rate or BPLR continue until repayment or renewal; they do not automatically convert to MCLR.
evidence: Existing loans and credit limits linked to the Base Rate / BPLR shall continue till repayment or renewal, as the case may be.

question: Under the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Interest Rates on Advances) Directions, 2025, may a commercial bank increase the credit risk premium charged to an existing borrower because the customer's credit risk profile has deteriorated?
answer: Yes. A commercial bank may increase the credit risk premium on an existing borrower's loan if the increase is attributable to deterioration in the customer's credit risk profile; a change in tenor premium is also an permitted ground.
evidence: The credit risk premium charged to an existing borrower shall not be increased except on account of deterioration in the credit risk profile of the customer or change in tenor premium.

question: What internal benchmark must a commercial bank use to price floating rate rupee loans that are sanctioned or renewed on or after April 1, 2016?
answer: The bank must use the Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR) as the internal benchmark for pricing such loans.
evidence: All floating rate rupee loans sanctioned and renewed w.e.f. April 1, 2016 shall be priced with reference to the Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR) which will be the internal benchmark

question: For a commercial bank, how should negative carry on mandatory CRR be calculated when returns on CRR balances are nil?
answer: Multiply the required CRR by the marginal cost of funds, then divide the result by one minus the CRR: Required CRR × marginal cost ÷ (1 − CRR).
evidence:
Negative carry on the mandatory CRR which arises due to return on CRR balances being nil, will be calculated as under:
Required CRR x (marginal cost) / (1- CRR)

question: Do the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Interest Rates on Advances) Directions, 2025 override or replace other existing laws and regulations that apply to commercial banks?

question: Under the RBI’s KYC customer acceptance requirements for NBFCs, is it permissible to deny a financial facility to a financially or socially disadvantaged member of the public, including a person with a disability?

evidence: The Customer Acceptance Policy shall not result in denial of a financial facility to members of the general public, especially those who are financially or socially disadvantaged, including the Persons with Disabilities (PwDs).

question: As a compliance officer at an NBFC that belongs to a group, am I required to implement group-wide anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing programmes?

question: As an NBFC, how often must we carry out a periodic review of the risk categorisation of our customer accounts?

question: When is an NBFC not required to identify and verify the beneficial owners of a legal person customer?

question: For an NBFC, who must approve the KYC policy, and can the Board delegate that responsibility?
answer: The Board of Directors must duly approve the NBFC’s KYC policy. Approval may instead be given by a committee to which the Board has delegated power.
evidence: (1) The NBFC shall have a KYC policy. The Board of Directors of the NBFC, or any committee to which the Board has delegated power, shall duly approve the KYC policy.

question: What must an NBFC do if a customer that is a non-profit organisation is not already registered on the DARPAN Portal of NITI Aayog?

question: As an NBFC, what must we put in place to manage money laundering and terrorist financing risks?

evidence: The NBFC shall apply a Risk Based Approach (RBA) for mitigation and management of the risks (identified on its own or through national risk assessment) and shall have Board-approved policies, controls and procedures in this regard.

question: How often must an NBFC check the UN sanctions lists and the domestic terrorism schedules for updates?

question: I'm an NBFC and a partnership firm wants to open an account with me. What documents do I need to collect?

question: When is an individual customer required to provide their Aadhaar number to an NBFC, and when is it voluntary?

question: Can an NBFC maintain a pooled account managed by a professional intermediary for a mutual fund or pension fund?

question: If an existing KYC-compliant customer of an NBFC wants to open a new account or avail a new product, does the NBFC need to perform a fresh CDD exercise for identification?

question: An NBFC offers monthly instalment (EMI) programmes on credit cards. Which regulatory directions govern these programmes, and do they fall within the scope of the Credit Facilities Directions?

question: What is the minimum length of the cooling-off period that an NBFC must allow for a digital loan?

question: What loan-to-value ratio must an NBFC with an asset size of ₹100 crore or more maintain when lending against listed shares, and how quickly must any shortfall be corrected?

question: As an NBFC that provides a default loss guarantee (DLG), how much of the outstanding guarantee must I deduct from my regulatory capital?

question: Can a Self-Regulatory Organisation representing NBFCs publish the range of interest rates charged by its member NBFCs on microfinance loans in a particular district as part of an awareness campaign?

question: For an NBFC, from what date do the RBI requirements for releasing original property documents after repayment or settlement of a personal loan apply?

question: What documents must an NBFC provide to borrowers when sanctioning or disbursing a loan?

question: As an NBFC, how frequently must we place a report on unclaimed gold or silver collateral before the Customer Service Committee or Board for review?

question: When is an NBFC required to release securities held as collateral for a loan?

question: As an NBFC offering loans secured by gold or silver, where must the pledged collateral be kept?

question: What details must an NBFC include in its loan application forms so that borrowers can meaningfully compare terms with other lenders and make informed decisions?
answer: The form must include all necessary information affecting the borrower's interest to enable comparison and informed decision-making.
evidence: Loan application forms shall include necessary information which affects the interest of the borrower, so that a meaningful comparison with the terms and conditions offered by another lender can be made, and informed decision can be taken by the borrower.

question: For an NBFC collecting microfinance loans, during what hours must it avoid calling borrowers, and what calling pattern is also prohibited?
answer: An NBFC must not persistently call a microfinance borrower, nor call that borrower before 9:00 a.m. or after 6:00 p.m.
evidence: Persistently calling the borrower and/ or calling the borrower before 9:00 a.m. and after 6:00 p.m.

question: What must an NBFC display on its website regarding the valuation of gold and silver collateral?
answer: An NBFC must display the methodology it uses to determine the net weight of gold and silver content in eligible collateral and the price used to value that content for calculating the loan-to-value ratio.
evidence: An NBFC shall display on its website the methodology adopted by it for determination of net weight of the gold and silver content of the eligible collateral and the price used to value the gold and silver content of the eligible collateral for determination of LTV ratio.

question: As an NBFC, where in our financial statements do we need to report the amount of fraud for the year?
answer: You must disclose the fraud amount reported in the company for the year in the Notes to Accounts of your Financial Statements.
evidence: The Applicable NBFC shall disclose the amount related to fraud reported in the company for the year in its Financial Statements – Notes to Accounts.

question: What must NBFCs in the Upper Layer and Middle Layer do to develop their Early Warning System for non-credit transactions?
answer: They must identify suitable indicators and parameterize them in their EWS system to monitor other financial and non-credit related transactions.
evidence: NBFCs - UL and ML shall develop / strengthen their EWS system by identifying suitable indicators and parameterising them in their EWS system for monitoring other financial / non-credit related transactions.

question: As an NBFC compliance officer, if our company took fraud risk management actions under the previous RBI directions that have now been repealed, do those actions remain valid and governed by the old rules?
answer: Yes, any action taken or initiated under the repealed directions continues to be governed by those provisions.
evidence: any action taken or purported to have been taken, or initiated under the repealed directions, instructions, or guidelines shall continue to be governed by the provisions thereof.

question: As an NBFC, when do the penal measures under Paragraphs 35 and 36 cease to apply to a borrower that has undergone resolution?
answer: The penal measures no longer apply once a Resolution Plan under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 or the applicable resolution framework has been implemented for that borrower.
evidence: The penal measures as detailed in Paragraphs 35 and 36 shall not be applicable to entities / business enterprises after implementation of the Resolution Plan under Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) or aforesaid resolution framework.

question: After an NBFC identifies a borrower's account as fraudulent, what must happen to borrowal accounts at other group companies that share a promoter or whole-time director?
answer: Those borrowal accounts must be subjected to examination from a fraud angle by the concerned Regulated Entities.
evidence: In case an account is identified as a fraud by any Applicable NBFC, the borrowal accounts of other group companies, in which one or more promoter(s) / whole-time director(s) are common, shall also be subjected to examination by Regulated Entities (REs) concerned from fraud angle under these Directions.

question: When can an NBFC close a fraud case under the Fraud Risk Management Directions?
answer: An NBFC can close a fraud case when the fraud cases pending with law enforcement agencies or courts are disposed of and the examination of staff accountability has been completed.
evidence: The fraud cases pending with LEAs / Court are disposed of; and (2) The examination of staff accountability has been completed.

question: What must an NBFC do if it suspects wrongdoing or fraudulent activity in an account?
answer: It must arrange further investigation of the account through either an external audit or an internal audit conducted under its Board-approved Policy.
evidence: 25. In case where there is a suspicion / indication of wrongdoing or fraudulent activity, the Applicable NBFC shall use an external audit or an internal audit as per its Board approved Policy for further investigation in such accounts.

question: As an NBFC, must we finish a fraud investigation before we transfer a loan account to another lender or to an Asset Reconstruction Company?
answer: Yes, the Applicable NBFC is required to complete the investigation from a fraud angle before transferring the loan account or credit facility to other lenders or ARCs.
evidence: The Applicable NBFC shall complete the investigation from fraud angle before transferring the loan account / credit facility to other lenders / Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs).

question: As an NBFC, by when must we report a robbery or attempted theft to the RBI?
answer: An NBFC must report the incident immediately and, in any event, no later than seven days after it occurs.
evidence: The Applicable NBFC shall report instances of theft, burglary, dacoity and robbery (including attempted cases), to Fraud Monitoring Group (FMG), Department of Supervision, Central Office, Reserve Bank of India, immediately (not later than seven days) from their occurrence

question: Under what circumstances can an NBFC withdraw a Fraud Monitoring Report (FMR) or remove a perpetrator's name from it?
answer: An NBFC may withdraw an FMR or remove a perpetrator's name only under exceptional circumstances, with due justification and approval from an official at least at the director level.
evidence: The Applicable NBFC may, under exceptional circumstances, withdraw FMR / remove name(s) of perpetrator(s) from FMR. Such withdrawal / removal shall, however, be made with due justification and with the approval of an official at least in the rank of a director.

question: What is the maximum fraud amount that an NBFC can close for statistical reporting purposes under the fraud risk management directions?
answer: An NBFC can close reported fraud cases involving amounts up to ₹25 lakh for limited statistical or reporting purposes.
evidence: NBFCs are allowed, for limited statistical / reporting purposes, to close those reported fraud cases involving amount up to ₹25 lakh

question: What areas must the internal audit function cover in an Applicable NBFC with respect to fraud risk management?
answer: Internal audit must cover controls and processes for prevention, detection, classification, monitoring, reporting, closure and withdrawal of fraud cases, as well as weaknesses in critical fraud risk management processes including delay in reporting, non-reporting, staff accountability examinations and prudential provisioning.
evidence: Internal Audit in the Applicable NBFC shall cover controls and processes involved in prevention, detection, classification, monitoring, reporting, closure and withdrawal of fraud cases, as well as weaknesses observed in the critical processes in the fraud risk management framework of the Applicable NBFC, including delay in reporting, non-reporting, conduct of staff accountability examination and prudential provisioning.

question: As an NBFC, at what minimum fraud amount must we report the incident to law enforcement agencies?
answer: An NBFC must mandatorily report incidents of fraud involving ₹1 lakh or more to law enforcement agencies. Under Section 33 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, only the offences listed in that Section are otherwise mandatorily reportable.
evidence: The Applicable NBFC is, however, advised to mandatorily report incidents of fraud involving an amount of ₹1 lakh or more to LEAs.

question: What must an NBFC include in its policy for engaging external auditors?
answer: The policy must cover due diligence, competency, and track record of the auditors, among other aspects.
evidence: The Applicable NBFC shall frame a policy on engagement of external auditors covering aspects such as due diligence, competency and track record of the auditors, among others.

question: As an NBFC compliance officer, can our agreements with third-party service providers include terms making them accountable when their wilful negligence or malpractice contributes to fraud?
answer: Yes. An NBFC may include necessary terms and conditions in its agreements with third-party service providers to hold them accountable where their wilful negligence or malpractice is found to be a causative factor for fraud.
evidence: Therefore, the Applicable NBFC may incorporate necessary terms and conditions in its agreements with third-party service providers to hold them accountable in situations where wilful negligence / malpractice by them is found to be a causative factor for fraud.

question: What is the procedure for examining the accountability of very senior executives like the MD & CEO in an NBFC under the Fraud Risk Management Directions?
answer: The Audit Committee of the Board (ACB) must initiate the examination and present it to the Board, and the concerned executives are barred from participating in that meeting.
evidence: the ACB shall initiate examination of its accountability and place it before the Board. Such executives shall not participate in the meeting of the Board / ACB / SCBMF in which its accountability is to be considered.

question: As an NBFC, what conditions do I need to satisfy to be classified as an NBFC-MFI under the RBI's microfinance institution directions?
answer: You must be a non-deposit taking NBFC and have at least 60 percent of your total assets, after netting off intangible assets, deployed towards microfinance loans on an ongoing basis.
evidence: “NBFC-MFI” means a non-deposit taking NBFC which has a minimum of 60 percent of its total assets (netted off by intangible assets) deployed towards “microfinance loans” on an ongoing basis.

question: Which entities are covered by the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Microfinance Institution) Directions, 2025?
answer: The Directions apply to every Non-Banking Financial Company – Microfinance Institution (NBFC-MFI) registered with the Reserve Bank under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
evidence: These Directions shall be applicable to every Non-Banking Financial Company – Microfinance Institution (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'NBFC-MFIs' and individually as an 'NBFC-MFI') registered with the Reserve Bank under the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Act No. 2 of 1934).

question: For an NBFC organized as a not-for-profit company that is not eligible for the referenced exemptions, what registration and compliance obligations apply?
answer: It must register as an NBFC-MFI, adhere to the regulations applicable to NBFC-MFIs, and submit its registration application to the Reserve Bank.
evidence: ‘Not for profit’ companies that are not eligible for the exemptions mentioned above are required to register as NBFC-MFIs and adhere to the regulations applicable to NBFC-MFIs. Such companies shall submit the application for registration as an NBFC-MFI to the Reserve Bank.

question: What provisioning norms must an NBFC-MFI follow for standard assets on its microfinance loans?
answer: An NBFC-MFI must apply the standard asset provisioning requirements specified in the RBI's Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning Directions, 2025 that correspond to the regulatory layer the NBFC-MFI falls under in the scale-based framework.
evidence: Standard assets provisioning of microfinance loans of an NBFC-MFI lying in a particular layer of the scale based regulatory framework shall be in accordance with instructions contained in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning) Directions, 2025 for the respective layer.

question: As an NBFC-MFI acting as a channelizing agent for a Central or State Government loan scheme, how should those scheme loans be treated when checking the minimum threshold of microfinance loans?
answer: They must be treated as a separate business segment, and the scheme loans must be excluded from both the microfinance-loan numerator and the total-assets denominator used to assess compliance with the minimum threshold.
evidence: Loans disbursed or managed by the NBFC-MFI in its capacity as channelizing agent for Central / State Government Agencies shall be considered as a separate business segment. These loans shall not be included either in the numerator (microfinance loans) or the denominator (total assets) for the purpose of determining compliance with the minimum threshold of microfinance loans.

question: What must an NBFC-MFI do regarding the treatment of deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities when computing its capital?
answer: An NBFC-MFI must follow the provisions of the RBI's Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy Directions, 2025 for the treatment of deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities for capital computation.
evidence: An NBFC-MFI shall also adhere to provisions of the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025 on treatment of deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities for computation of capital.

question: What must an NBFC follow when working out the capital adequacy treatment of its on-balance and off-balance sheet assets?
answer: An NBFC must apply the treatment set out in the RBI's (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025 for both on-balance and off-balance sheet assets.
evidence: The treatment to on-balance and off-balance sheet assets for capital adequacy shall be as provided in the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025 respectively.

question: Which Reserve Bank of India directions on credit facilities must an NBFC-MFI comply with?
answer: An NBFC-MFI must comply with the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
evidence: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.

question: As an NBFC-MFI, what regulatory requirements must we follow when declaring dividends?
answer: An NBFC-MFI must adhere to the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Declaration of Dividends) Directions, 2025.
evidence: An NBFC-MFI shall adhere to the provisions of Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Declaration of Dividends) Directions, 2025.

question: Which other Reserve Bank of India directions on income recognition, asset classification and provisioning apply to an NBFC-MFI?
answer: The Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning) Directions, 2025 apply to NBFC-MFIs, except where they contradict the NBFC-MFI Directions.
evidence: All other provisions contained in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning) Directions, 2025, where not contradictory to the contents of these directions, shall be applicable to NBFC-MFIs.

question: As an NBFC-MFI, what must I follow when opening a branch or representative office, setting up a subsidiary or joint venture, or undertaking an investment abroad?
answer: You must adhere to paragraphs 15 to 19 of the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Undertaking of Financial Services) Directions, 2025.
evidence: An NBFC-MFI shall adhere to the provisions contained in paragraphs 15 to 19 of the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Undertaking of Financial Services) Directions, 2025.

question: What is the maximum share of total assets that an NBFC which is not registered as an NBFC-MFI may allocate to microfinance loans?
answer: Such an NBFC may extend microfinance loans only up to 25 per cent of its total assets in aggregate.
evidence: An NBFC, which does not qualify as an NBFC-MFI shall extend microfinance loans, which in aggregate does not exceed 25 per cent of its total assets.

question: For an NBFC covered by the RBI's Non-Banking Financial Company–Microfinance Institution Directions, 2025, what qualifies as a standard asset?
answer: For an NBFC, a standard asset is one with no perceived default in repayment of principal or payment of interest. It must also disclose no problem and carry no more than the normal risk associated with the business.
evidence: Standard asset means the asset in respect of which, no default in repayment of principal or payment of interest is perceived and which does not disclose any problem nor carry more than normal risk attached to the business.

question: What is the minimum capital adequacy ratio that an NBFC-MFI must maintain under the RBI directions?
answer: An NBFC-MFI must maintain a capital adequacy ratio of at least 15 percent of its aggregate risk weighted assets and risk adjusted off-balance sheet items.
evidence: An NBFC-MFI shall maintain a capital adequacy ratio consisting of Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital which shall not be less than 15 per cent of its aggregate risk weighted assets of on-balance sheet and of risk adjusted value of off-balance sheet items.

question: Under the RBI's NBFC-MFI Directions, 2025, do the other RBI directions apply to every NBFC-MFI in the same way?

question: What IT governance framework must an NBFC-P2P lending platform comply with?
answer: An NBFC-P2P must comply with the Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices dated November 07, 2023, as amended from time to time.
evidence: An NBFC-P2P shall comply with Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices dated November 07, 2023 (as amended from time to time).

question: As an NBFC, what oversight must our Board put in place for our Fair Practices Code and grievance-redressal arrangements?
answer: The Board must arrange periodic reviews of Fair Practices Code compliance and how the grievance-redressal mechanism operates at various management levels. It must receive a consolidated report of those reviews at regular intervals prescribed by the Board.
evidence: The Board of Directors shall also provide for periodic review of the compliance of the Fair Practices Code and the functioning of the grievances redressal mechanism at various levels of management. A consolidated report of such reviews shall be submitted to the Board at regular intervals, as may be prescribed by it.

question: As an NBFC-P2P, how many escrow accounts must we maintain and what are their designated purposes under the fund transfer mechanism?
answer: An NBFC-P2P must maintain at least two escrow accounts: a Lenders' Escrow Account for funds received from lenders pending disbursal, and a Borrowers' Escrow Account for collections from borrowers.
evidence: At least two escrow accounts, one for funds received from lenders and pending disbursal (i.e., Lenders’ escrow Account), and the other for collections from borrowers (i.e., Borrowers’ escrow Account), shall be maintained.

question: For an NBFC-P2P, at what shareholding level does an allotment of shares require the Reserve Bank’s prior written permission?
answer: Prior written permission is required when an allotment would take an individual’s or group’s aggregate holding to 26% or more of the NBFC-P2P’s paid-up capital.
evidence: any allotment of shares which will take the aggregate holding of an individual or group to equivalent of 26 per cent and more of the paid-up capital of the NBFC-P2P;

question: How often must an NBFC-P2P conduct an information system audit of its internal systems and processes?
answer: An NBFC-P2P must conduct an information system audit at least once every two years.
evidence: Information System Audit of the internal systems and processes shall be in place and shall be conducted at least once in two years

question: As an NBFC-P2P, are we allowed to follow the RBI's Guidance Note on Operational Risk Management and Operational Resilience?
answer: Yes. An NBFC-P2P may make use of the Guidance Note on Operational Risk Management and Operational Resilience, including any amendments made to it from time to time.
evidence: An NBFC-P2P may make use of the ‘ Guidance Note on Operational Risk Management and Operational Resilience’, as amended from time to time.

question: As an NBFC-P2P, must I comply with the other RBI directions referenced in paragraph 4 in addition to these Peer-to-Peer Lending Platform Directions?
answer: Yes, the NBFC-P2P Directions apply in addition to, and not as a substitute for, the other relevant instructions mentioned in paragraph 4.
evidence: the instructions contained in these Directions shall be applicable to an NBFC-P2P in addition and not in substitution to the other relevant instructions contained in the directions mentioned in paragraph 4 above

question: May the RBI impose additional conditions for registering an NBFC peer-to-peer lending platform beyond the standard eligibility requirements?
answer: Yes. The RBI may specify any additional condition it considers necessary to ensure that the commencement or continuation of the business in India will not be prejudicial to the public interest.
evidence: (9) Any other condition as may be specified by the Reserve Bank, fulfillment of which, in the opinion of the Reserve Bank, is necessary to ensure that the commencement of or carrying on the business in India shall not be prejudicial to the public interest.

question: What are the credit information reporting obligations for an NBFC-P2P platform regarding borrower transactions?
answer: An NBFC-P2P must comply with the RBI's Credit Information Reporting Directions, 2025 for reporting and updating credit information related to borrower transactions on its platform.
evidence: An NBFC-P2P shall comply with the relevant instructions, as applicable, in the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Credit Information Reporting) Directions, 2025 for reporting and updating the credit information relating to borrower transactions on the platform.

question: For an NBFC-P2P, how is the leverage ratio calculated?
answer: The leverage ratio is calculated by dividing the NBFC-P2P’s total outside liabilities by its owned funds.
evidence: “Leverage Ratio” means the Total Outside Liabilities divided by Owned Funds, of the NBFC-P2P.

question: As a lender on an NBFC-P2P platform, can the platform hold my lent funds on its own balance sheet?
answer: No, an NBFC-P2P platform is prohibited from holding funds received from lenders for lending on its own balance sheet.
evidence: not hold on its own balance sheet, funds received from lenders for lending, or funds received from borrowers for servicing loans, or such funds as stipulated in paragraphs 37 and 38 of these Directions

question: As a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) operating a peer-to-peer lending platform, do the RBI's 2025 P2P Lending Platform Directions replace other laws, rules, regulations, or directions that apply to my business?
answer: No. The RBI framework is additional to other applicable requirements and does not derogate from them, so those requirements continue to apply alongside it.
evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

question: What changes is an NBFC-P2P required to communicate to the Reserve Bank of India?
answer: An NBFC-P2P must communicate changes in address, directors, auditors, and similar matters as specified in the referenced directions.
evidence: Every NBFC-P2P shall communicate change of address, directors, auditors, etc., as prescribed in paragraphs 6 and 7 of Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Miscellaneous) Directions, 2025.

question: What must an NBFC-P2P do to meet the RBI requirements concerning acquisition of shareholding or control?
answer: It must comply with the instructions in paragraphs 8 to 10 of the RBI’s Non-Banking Financial Companies – Acquisition of Shareholding or Control Directions, 2025.
evidence: An NBFC-P2P shall comply with the instructions as prescribed in paragraphs 8 to 10 of Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Acquisition of Shareholding or Control) Directions, 2025.

question: What must an NBFC-P2P do regarding a Fair Practices Code and Board approval?
answer: An NBFC-P2P must establish a Fair Practices Code based on the Guidelines in the Directions and obtain approval for it from its Board.
evidence: An NBFC-P2P shall put in place a Fair Practices Code, based on the Guidelines outlined herein, with the approval of its Board.

question: For an NBFC-AA, what is the minimum number of Board members required on its Nomination Committee?
answer: The Nomination Committee must have at least three members from the Board of Directors.
evidence: NBFC-AA shall form a Nomination Committee consisting of not less than three members of its Board of Directors to ensure 'fit and proper' status of proposed/ existing directors.

question: As a compliance officer at an NBFC-AA, which disclosure framework must I follow and are there any specific exemptions from the standard NBFC financial statement directions?
answer: An NBFC-AA must comply with the disclosure requirements in the RBI's NBFC Financial Statements Presentation and Disclosures Directions, 2025, except for the provisions in paragraphs 13 to 15 and paragraph 20.
evidence: NBFC-AA shall comply with the disclosure requirements specified in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Financial Statements: Presentation and Disclosures) Directions, 2025, except provisions contained in paragraphs 13 to 15 and paragraph 20.

question: What changes should an NBFC-AA submit information about?

question: To which entities do the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Account Aggregator) Directions, 2025 apply?

evidence: These Directions shall be applicable to Non-Banking Financial Companies – Account Aggregators (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'NBFC-AAs' and individually as an 'NBFC-AA').

question: For an NBFC operating as an Account Aggregator (NBFC-AA), must it follow the RBI's Account Aggregator Directions as well as the other relevant NBFC directions, rather than treating the Account Aggregator requirements as a replacement?

evidence: Notwithstanding the above, the instructions contained in these Directions shall be applicable to an NBFC-AA in addition and not in substitution to the other relevant instructions contained in the directions mentioned in paragraph 4 above.

question: Who has the final authority to interpret the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Account Aggregator) Directions, 2025?
answer: The Reserve Bank of India's interpretation of any provision of these Directions is final and binding.
evidence: the interpretation of any provision of these Directions given by the RBI shall be final and binding

question: Our NBFC has joined the Account Aggregator ecosystem as a Financial Information User. May we use or share customer financial information received through an NBFC-AA for purposes that go beyond what the customer's consent artefact allows?

question: As a compliance officer at an NBFC-AA, which regulatory layer under the Scale Based Regulation framework applies to my company?
answer: An NBFC-AA must always remain in the Base Layer of the regulatory structure under the Scale Based Regulation for NBFCs.
evidence: NBFC-AA shall always remain in the Base Layer of the regulatory structure specified in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Registration, Exemptions and Framework for Scale Based Regulation) Directions, 2025.

question: What must an NBFC Account Aggregator do to ensure its IT systems remain suitable as the RBI updates its Account Aggregator requirements?

question: What details must a standardized consent artefact obtained by an NBFC-AA include?
answer: The artefact must include the customer's identity and optional contact information, the nature and purpose of the financial information requested, the identity of any recipients, a notification URL, the consent creation and expiry dates, and the NBFC-AA's identity and signature or digital signature.

question: As an NBFC, must I follow the Reserve Bank of India's Non-Banking Financial Companies (Account Aggregator) Directions, 2025 in addition to other laws, rules, regulations, and directions that apply to me?
answer: Yes. The Account Aggregator Directions supplement, rather than replace or weaken, other applicable laws, rules, regulations, and directions in force.
evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

question: If our NBFC operates as an Account Aggregator, are we allowed to use the financial information we collect from customers for any purpose other than providing account aggregation services?

question: If our NBFC applies to become an Account Aggregator with less than ₹2 crore in net owned fund, can it still obtain registration?

question: Can the Reserve Bank of India issue clarifications on the Account Aggregator Directions that become binding on NBFCs?
answer: Yes, the Reserve Bank can issue clarifications on the directions, and such clarifications are treated as part of the directions themselves.
evidence: The Reserve Bank can give any clarification in respect of the above directions and such clarification shall be treated as part of these directions.

question: When an NBFC receives a customer’s request to correct inaccurate information in a credit information report, who is responsible for making the correction?

question: As a compliance officer at an NBFC, who is responsible for selecting the members of the Standing Sub-Group of the Technical Working Group under the Credit Information Reporting Directions?

evidence: Members of the Sub-Group shall be selected by the convenor with prior approval of the Reserve Bank.

question: As an NBFC acting as a CI, what must be included in its loan policies and credit appraisal processes?

evidence: A CI shall include in their loan policies / credit appraisal processes, suitable provisions for obtaining CIRs from one or more CICs so that the credit decisions are based on credit information available in the system.
